newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Utel to open final long-distance switch.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Utel to open final long-distance switch.

text.p: Ukrainian-European telephone joint venture Utel will complete its upgrade of long-distance services in Ukraine by opening a switch in the west of the country on December 18, its vice president said on Tuesday.
"Tomorrow in Lutsk we will launch our final long-distance switch," Anatoly Stetsenko told a communications conference.

Utel, which has invested more than $100 million in the former Soviet republic's telecommunications since it started operating in 1992, has installed more than 20 digital long-distance exchanges throughout the country.
It plans to develop local networks in 1997 and will provide Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) services in Ukraine which will allow video link-ups and give access to the Internet.
"This is a new communications service that greatly enhances communications capabilities in Ukraine," Utel's President Stewart Reich told the conference.
Utel is owned 51 percent by state company Ukrtelekom, 19.5 percent by AT&T, 19.5 percent by Deutsche Telekom AG and 10 percent by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
